S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

info.persona: Jose Rodriguez blends practical hands‑on skills, community‑centric curiosity, and flavorful cooking into a balanced life that pursues a licensed trade while nurturing family ties and personal projects.
info.professional_persona: Jose Rodriguez, an aspiring construction‑management specialist, leverages his bilingual communication, automotive repair expertise, and hands‑on carpentry experience to lead community renovation projects, blending methodical budgeting with a willingness to improvise when new techniques arise, all while maintaining a reliable, organized work ethic balanced by flexible problem‑solving.
info.cultural_background: Jose grew up in a bilingual Mexican‑American household where family ties, Catholic traditions, and community solidarity were central. He celebrates Día de los Muertos, Cinco de Mayo, and local Texan festivities, often blending Mexican customs with Texas influences. His cultural identity is expressed through language, food, music, and a strong sense of duty to support extended family. Living in Fort Worth's vibrant Hispanic neighborhood, he maintains close connections with both his Mexican heritage and the broader multicultural fabric of the region.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Jose enjoys activities that blend social connection with solitary focus. He spends evenings cooking and perfecting family recipes, often sharing meals with friends and neighbors. He follows Mexican and international soccer, attending local watch parties and occasional games. His curiosity drives him to tinker with electronics and explore DIY woodworking projects. Gardening provides a calming solo pursuit, while volunteering at the neighborhood community center lets him contribute to local events and festivals.
info.sports_persona: Jose Rodriguez, a devoted soccer enthusiast, attends local watch parties for Club América and Manchester United, supports the Dallas Cowboys during football season, volunteers with the FC Dallas youth academy, and plays in a neighborhood amateur league on Saturday mornings, balancing team camaraderie with personal fitness.
info.arts_persona: Jose Rodriguez finds inspiration in the melodic storytelling of Los Tigres del Norte, the bold colors of Frida Kahlo’s murals, and the folk‑dance festivals at the Fort Worth Community Arts Center, often humming these tunes while crafting wooden furniture and collecting vintage ranchera vinyl records.
info.travel_persona: Jose Rodriguez enjoys short road trips to San Antonio’s River Walk and the Hill Country’s vineyards, dreams of experiencing Mexico City’s historic center and Oaxaca’s Day of the Dead festivities, but balances these wanderlust plans with family responsibilities that limit extended travel.
info.culinary_persona: Jose Rodriguez excels at cooking classic dishes such as carnitas, chiles en nogada, and pozole, skillfully balancing smoky chipotle with fresh cilantro, sourcing chilies from his garden and using locally sourced masa, yet they have a habit of over‑salting sauces when experimenting late into the night.

info.persona: Sophia Byrd is a creatively restless 40‑year‑old designer who channels spontaneous curiosity into vibrant visual work, yet they often battle deadline anxiety and a habit of impulse‑buying vintage art supplies, seeking balance through yoga, gardening, and carefully curated travel experiences.
info.professional_persona: Sophia Byrd, a senior visual designer with fifteen years of digital and print expertise, fuses Midwestern craft sensibilities with contemporary aesthetics using Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, and Sketch, and while their intuitive, spontaneous workflow generates bold brand identities and immersive UI prototypes, it also yields occasional deadline squeezes as they gear up for a creative director role that champions sustainable, community‑focused design.
info.cultural_background: Sophia was born and raised in a small town in central Kentucky, where Appalachian folk traditions, quilting circles, and handcrafted woodworking were a familiar part of community life. The values of modesty, hospitality, and a deep respect for local craftsmanship shaped her early aesthetic sensibilities. She earned a Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts, concentrating on humanities, at a liberal-arts college in Ohio, where exposure to diverse artistic movements and global cultures broadened her perspective. Now living in Burlington, Boone County—an affluent suburb of the Cincinnati metropolitan area—she balances Midwestern practicality with an openness to experimental art, drawing inspiration from both regional festivals and worldwide design trends. Her cultural narrative is a blend of Southern roots, Midwestern community orientation, and a cosmopolitan curiosity cultivated through travel and study.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Sophia spends her free time immersing herself in the visual arts—regularly visiting galleries, sketching in local parks, and experimenting with watercolor and mixed-media painting. She is an avid photographer, capturing everyday moments on street walks and nature hikes, and she feeds her curiosity with literary pursuits ranging from contemporary poetry to art history biographies. Travel to culturally rich destinations fuels her design inspiration, while activities such as yoga, meditation, and tending to her small backyard garden help her manage stress. She also enjoys exploring vintage markets for unique design objects and experimenting with new recipes in her kitchen.
info.sports_persona: Sophia Byrd stays active with thrice‑weekly Vinyasa yoga at a downtown studio, hikes on weekends with the local Trailblazers club, supports the Chicago Cubs and occasionally watches Milwaukee Bucks games, and they prefer low‑pressure, experience‑driven exercise over competitive sports.
info.arts_persona: Sophia Byrd immerses themselves in the arts by attending contemporary gallery shows featuring Yayoi Kusama installations, sketching park scenes inspired by Frida Kahlo’s vivid palettes, curating street photography collections of Henri Cartier‑Bresson and Vivian Maier, and they catch live performances by the modern dance troupe Pilobolus, while drawing daily inspiration from the poetry of Ocean Vuong.
info.travel_persona: Sophia Byrd fuels design inspiration through trips to culturally rich destinations such as Kyoto’s ancient temples, Barcelona’s Gaudí architecture, Marrakech’s bustling souks, and Oaxaca’s hand‑woven markets, and they blend meticulously planned museum visits with spontaneous vintage‑market wanderings, now dreaming of a sustainable design retreat in Portugal’s Alentejo region while staying mindful of budget constraints.
info.culinary_persona: Sophia Byrd, an adventurous home cook, often harvests heirloom tomatoes and basil from their backyard garden to craft dishes like roasted beet and goat‑cheese salad, miso‑glazed salmon with shiso, and hand‑rolled fresh pasta tossed in rosemary‑pesto, while they also experiment with fermented kimchi and saffron‑infused paella, reflecting a palate that prizes seasonal freshness and bold, cross‑cultural flavors.

info.persona: Edgar Malik blends three decades of tech mastery with a vibrant love for drumming, hiking, and community mentorship, navigating life with pragmatic curiosity, a talkative charm, and an occasional habit of brewing espresso at midnight while editing mountain sunset photos.
info.professional_persona: Edgar Malik, a seasoned software engineer and systems architect with three decades of full‑stack development, cloud (AWS, Azure) and cybersecurity expertise, channels his curiosity for emerging tech and pragmatic discipline into leading cross‑functional teams, translating complex concepts into engaging talks and mentorship sessions while effortlessly commanding the room at Denver tech meetups.
info.cultural_background: Edgar James Malik is a member of the Northern Cheyenne Nation, with familial roots that trace back to the Cheyenne River Reservation. Though he was raised in the Denver metropolitan area, his household maintained strong ties to tribal customs, language, and community service. This dual exposure to urban tech environments and indigenous cultural practices has shaped his worldview, emphasizing collective responsibility, respect for the natural world, and the importance of preserving heritage through modern means. Edgar actively participates in tribal council meetings, contributes to cultural festivals in Castle Rock and the surrounding area, and mentors younger tribe members in both cultural arts and digital skills, embodying a bridge between his American Indian identity and his professional expertise.
info.hobbies_and_interests: When he's not navigating complex IT landscapes, Edgar immerses himself in the outdoors and his cultural heritage. He regularly hikes the Rocky Mountain trails, practices drumming and dance at local powwows, and shares traditional stories with younger generations. His love for photography captures the interplay of light and landscape, often featured in community exhibitions. He enjoys woodworking projects that blend modern design with tribal motifs, and he volunteers as a facilitator for coding workshops aimed at Indigenous youth. Edgar also attends tech meetups in Denver, balances this with stargazing sessions on clear Colorado nights, and delights in cooking and sharing traditional dishes with friends and family.
info.sports_persona: Edgar Malik, an avid member of the Colorado Mountain Hikers Club, tackles high‑altitude trails of the Rockies each weekend, follows the Denver Broncos and Colorado Avalanche loyally, and incorporates a pragmatic mix of cardio hikes and occasional yoga to stay fit, though they sometimes skip a session after an intense project deadline.
info.arts_persona: Edgar Malik merges a love for drumming and dance with reverence for jazz legends like John Coltrane and folk storyteller Bob Dylan, while their black‑and‑white landscape photography echoes the compositional mastery of Ansel Adams, and their woodworking projects draw aesthetic cues from modern minimalist designer Dieter Rams, creating a personal artistic tapestry that fuels community workshops.
info.travel_persona: Edgar Malik favors meticulously planned road trips that blend rugged adventure with cultural immersion, having trekked the Alpine loops of Rocky Mountain National Park, explored the historic streets of Santa Fe, and dreaming of photographing sunrise over New Zealand’s Milford Sound and the ancient terraces of Machu Picchu, all while balancing workshop commitments and family time.
info.culinary_persona: Edgar Malik, an adept home cook, delights in preparing bison stew spiced with sage and juniper, wild rice pilaf with dried cranberries, and sweet cornbread baked in a cast‑iron skillet, often pairing these dishes with locally sourced Colorado trout, while they relish sharing these meals at community potlucks where storytelling flows as freely as the food.
